explanation: Work from the bottom upwards. The best path starting at a cell is its weight plus the smaller of the two reachable child costs; one array stores the active row of costs.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The bottom row stores exact costs for paths beginning there. For each higher cell, every allowed path must next choose one of its two children, so adding that cell’s weight to the smaller child cost gives its exact optimum. Induction upwards reaches the optimum at the top.
walkthrough: For triangle [[3],[4,1],[2,8,5]], the row above the bottom gets costs [4+min(2,8),1+min(8,5)]=[6,6]. The top adds 3, giving minimum 9.
edgeCases: Negative weights do not invalidate the recurrence.
One row returns its only entry.
Only the two children directly below a cell are reachable.
